prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity desktop web app decision comp at exactly 1440 × 900 pixels, showing the first viewport of a shipped Frank Ad Radar operator screen.
Input image: Image 1 is the edit target and authoritative visual reference for the incumbent Frank Window shell. Preserve its straight-on white one-viewport structure, exact 220px left rail, top bar, Frank logo and wordmark character, Inter workhorse typography, spacing, flat controls, and hairline component language. Replace the Hub content with Ad Radar content; do not reuse the Hub message composer or any Ad Studio content.

Primary request: Design the “Observation Timeline” working surface for Frank Ad Radar, as a practical dense operator screen rather than a poster.
Composition, in order:
1. Keep a fixed 220px left rail from Image 1. Show FRANK at the top, WORKSPACE with Hub, PROJECTS with “Perth Growth” as current project context, and WINDOW items Files, Tools, Ad Studio, Ad Radar, Trace, Releases. Ad Radar is selected with one tiny red active dot; rail items remain flat.
2. Across the main column, make a compact run and freshness header about 74px high. Show “Ad Radar” and “Observation timeline”, project “Perth Growth”, “HRM-24A7 · SYNTHETIC FIXTURE”, “Runs on Hermes”, “Last observation 32s ago”, and a small black pill action “Open run”. Make ownership truthful: Frank shows durable state; Hermes owns the run.
3. Directly beneath, add one thin pinned-filter ledger about 46px high: label “PINNED FILTERS” and compact chips “Changed today”, “Quarantined”, “Perth”, “Video”, plus “Save filter”.
4. Use the remaining height as one continuous workspace split into a wide chronological observation rail and a fixed right inspector about 420px wide. The observation rail is the dominant full-height navigation, not a card grid. Use a fine vertical chronology line, precise tabular timestamps, compact event rows, small neutral status labels, advertiser/page names, and one-line evidence summaries. Include, in descending order: “changed” at 10:42 for Northline Homes, “new” at 10:38 for Kin & Coast, “quarantined” at 10:29 for Belmore Living, “approved” at 09:54 for Wattle & Frame, “stopped” at 09:31 for Solway Homes, and “published” at 09:14 for Fern & Field. The selected 10:42 changed event is clear through weight and neutral surface treatment, never a colorful slab. Show that the list scrolls internally.
5. The fixed right inspector opens the selected event. At top, show “CHANGED · 10:42:18” and “Northline Homes”. Include a real-looking synthetic ad thumbnail: muted natural photography of a modern coastal home, no promotional claim, with a small explicit label “SYNTHETIC CREATIVE”. Natural photographic color may appear only inside this media thumbnail. Below it, use crisp labeled sections and compact facts: “Public source observation” with “Meta Ad Library”, a synthetic source id, page and advertiser; “Classification” with image, residential, lifestyle hook, feed placement; “Media QA” with capture complete, dimensions verified, crop clear; “Provenance” with observation, classification and media reference ids; and “Receipts” with run, command and event ids. Include a black pill action “Add to compare” and a quiet text action “Open public record”.
6. Pin a small compare tray above the bottom edge of the chronology pane so volume never buries comparison. Label it “COMPARE · 2”, show two tiny media thumbnails with short identifiers, and a compact “Open compare” action. It must feel like one slim utility tray, not another app shell.

Visual system: pure #FFFFFF ground; #111111 ink; #666666 secondary; #999999 faint; #ECECEC hairlines; #F5F5F5 neutral chips. #E53C1F appears only in the slash of the Frank mark and the single selected rail dot—nowhere else in the UI. Inter only. Headings medium weight, labels 10–13px, dense readable operator typography, tabular numerals, exact alignment, generous whitespace only where it improves scanning. Flat white panes separated by 1px hairlines; restrained 8px and 12px radii only on controls and media. One viewport, no page scroll.

Text quality: all visible labels above must be correctly spelled, legible, and coherent. Use real product language and clearly marked synthetic fixture data. Do not invent prices, benchmarks, customer claims, performance claims, production counts, or production dates.

Avoid: gradients, glass, blur effects, shadows as decoration, bento cards, metric-card dashboards, charts, dark mode, colorful status coding, giant hero type, poster composition, illustration replacing the app, device frames, perspective, a second app shell, duplicated navigation, Ad Studio content, commercial ad claims, watermarks, gibberish filler text, or tiny unreadable labels.
Output intent: a polished straight-on screenshot of a believable shipped desktop operator UI, full fidelity and immediately readable at 1440 × 900.
